one_liner: md4c CommonMark parser and HTML renderer compiled to 31 kB-gzipped WebAssembly; about 2.3-2.4x markdown-it throughput.
what_it_does: Converts Markdown to HTML or XHTML in Node and browsers with one call, parse(source, options), backed by the C md4c parser compiled with Emscripten. Input may be a JS string or UTF-8 bytes. Output is a string by default, or with bytes: true a Uint8Array view into wasm memory. ParseFlags select md4c extensions, and an onCodeBlock callback can replace fenced-code output. It is a function-level substitute for marked(str) or markdownit.render(str), but it has no plugin system, token stream or AST.
how_it_is_fast: md4c is a single-pass, SAX-style C parser: it emits enter/leave/text callbacks straight into an HTML formatter that appends to one growable byte buffer reserved at 2x the input size. It never builds a JS object tree, so there is no per-node allocation or GC pressure. The JS boundary costs one copy of the input into the wasm heap, plus a TextDecoder pass on the output unless bytes: true is set, which is why the gap is widest on small inputs used in bytes mode.
when_to_use: Server-side or build-time rendering of trusted CommonMark/GFM-style Markdown to HTML in Node, where no markdown-it or marked plugins are needed and throughput matters (about 2.4x markdown-it 14 on the 200 KB CommonMark spec in md4w's run)
High volumes of small documents (comments, chat messages, README snippets), especially if the HTML can stay as bytes (bytes: true) and go straight to a socket or file
Browser bundles that want a small zero-dependency renderer (31 kB gzipped per the README)
Simple custom code-block rendering through the synchronous onCodeBlock hook
when_not_to_use: You depend on markdown-it or marked plugins, custom renderer rules, or a token stream or AST: only HTML/XHTML output is offered
Untrusted input without a separate sanitizer: raw HTML passes through unless ParseFlags.NO_HTML is set, and the URI filter only drops hrefs that start with 'javascript:' (case-insensitive)

You need a maintained package: the last commit is 2021-07-06, md4c is pinned to an October 2020 commit plus patches, and 8 issues are open, including ESM loading failing in the browser (#26), Cloudflare Workers support (#25) and async onCodeBlock (#28). md4w covers these.

Output must match the CommonMark reference renderer: every heading gets an injected <a id=... class="anchor"> slug link (issue #22 asks to disable it), and ParseFlags.DEFAULT turns on tables, strikethrough, task lists, permissive autolinks/ATX headers and whitespace collapsing (pass parseFlags: 0 for plain CommonMark)

integration.form: module (npm markdown-wasm 1.2.0: Node CommonJS file with embedded compressed wasm, UMD browser script with sidecar markdown.wasm, ES module with separate wasm)
integration.dependencies: none at runtime; building needs wasmc (an Emscripten emcc wrapper)
integration.min_toolchain: Any JS runtime with WebAssembly and TextEncoder/TextDecoder (published numbers on Node 14.11; no engines field). Rebuilding needs wasmc ^2.2.1 and Emscripten (emcc version not documented); release cflags are only -DMD4C_USE_UTF8.
integration.platforms: Node and browsers via wasm. Known gaps: the ES build fetches 'markdown.wasm' relative to the page rather than the module (#26), Cloudflare Workers is unsupported (#25), and 'TypeError: Cannot set property exports of undefined' is reported (#18).
integration.thread_safety: Single-threaded per instance: parse() reuses one static output buffer in wasm memory, so a bytes: true result is overwritten by the next parse() call (README says to slice() it); use one module instance per worker
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — parse(string) returns an HTML string like marked(str) or markdownit.render(str), but there are no plugins or renderer overrides, the extension set differs, and headings always gain anchor links, so the HTML is not byte-identical

gotchas: Benchmark harness flaws (test/benchmark/bench.js and graph.js). Only markdown-wasm gets bytes in and bytes out: parse(Buffer, {asMemoryView: true}) skips the TextEncoder on input and the TextDecoder on output, while the four JS libraries take and return strings. A commented-out 'markdown-wasm/string' row exists, and a 2020-10-16 commit titled 'benchmark: remove unused markdown-wasm/string' dropped it before the charts were published. The headline 'average ops/s' is an unweighted mean of per-file ops/s over 27 sample files, 24 of them 64-730 bytes, so it mostly measures per-call overhead, where skipping the string conversion helps most. Output is never compared across libraries.

The README charts are stale: avg-ops-per-sec.svg was last touched on 2020-10-16 ('new benchmarks after upgrading md4c'), before the v1.1.0 release and before the 2021-07-01 commits that upgraded wasmc to 2.2.1, added the javascript: URI filter and added onCodeBlock. The record's compiler note (wasmc ^2.2.1) describes the current package.json, not the measured build. The baselines are markdown-it 10 and marked 0.7.

Latent use-after-free in heading anchors (src/fmt_html.c, text_callback). slugptr is captured from r->outbuf->ptr before WBufAppendSlug, render_literal and WBufReserve run, and each of those can realloc the output buffer (WBufGrow). The slug is then memcpy'd from the possibly freed old buffer, so when growth moves the buffer, the href='#...' of a heading can receive stale heap bytes. That is wrong output and possibly fragments of earlier documents, not a sandbox escape. The bug does not affect the timing.

bytes: true and the deprecated asMemoryView return a view that is only valid until the next parse(). onCodeBlock bridges JS and wasm for every code block, which the README says hurts performance, and its return value is inserted unescaped.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: md4w wraps the same md4c core with Zig glue, is maintained, supports streaming and JSON output and runs on Cloudflare Workers, and measured about 1.14x faster than markdown-wasm in its own Deno run, so prefer it for new code. Pick markdown-wasm only for its single-file Node build with embedded wasm, its stable 2021 API or onCodeBlock. sparkdown (pulldown-cmark in wasm) is the alternative if you want a Rust parser compared against remark.
verified_claims_summary: Author's own run, charts dated 2020-10-16, on a 2.9 GHz MacBook with macOS 10.15 and Node 14.11, markdown-wasm in bytes-in/bytes-out mode. Over the 27 commonmark.js bench samples it averaged 195,065 parse+render ops/s vs 84,774 for markdown-it 10 (commonmark preset, IDNA link encoding disabled), 76,942 for marked 0.7, 66,185 for commonmark.js 0.29 and 8,502 for showdown 1.9 (2.3x over markdown-it, derived from page data). Mean throughput was 49 vs 17 MB/s (graph.js divides by 1,024,000). The md4w repo's run (Apple M1, Deno 1.40.5, 200 KB commonmark-spec.md, string output, markdown-wasm-es 1.2.1, a repackaging of 1.2) shows 2.16 vs 5.19 ms/iter against markdown-it 14.0.0 (2.4x, derived from page data), so the direction holds without the bytes-mode advantage.
status_note: Abandoned since 2021-07-06 (npm 1.2.0 published 2021-07-01; 1.7k stars, 69 forks, 2 open PRs, 8 open issues). MIT and small, so it is usable as a frozen dependency for trusted input. md4w is the maintained successor on the same md4c core. Reading the code turned up a heading-anchor use-after-free, and the benchmark harness favours markdown-wasm (bytes-only mode, string row removed, mean dominated by sub-KB files).
